bindwell_yields.speaker: narrator
bindwell_yields.text: The old needle lay down on the boards he'd sewn, and didn't get up. The seams in the floor went slack, one by one.

bindwell_yields.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_yields.text: Go on, then. Cut the thread. It's what I'd have done.

bindwell_yields.speaker: patch
bindwell_yields.text: You sewed the spine shut. The night of the flood. Everyone down there was knocking.

bindwell_yields.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_yields.text: I heard them. Every one. I had the high pages to think of, and the water was coming up the binding, and I thought: if I open it, we all go.

bindwell_yields.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_yields.text: So I sewed. Kettle stitch, all the way up. I sewed until my eye bled thread, and I didn't stop when the knocking did.

bindwell_yields.speaker: patch
bindwell_yields.text: I'm not going to cut you.

bindwell_yields.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_yields.text: Then you're a fool, fox. Or you've done something of your own you can't put down.

bindwell_yields.speaker: patch
bindwell_yields.text: Come down to the Spine. There's a stove. The pages need sewing back together, and you're the only one who knows how they were sewn apart.

bindwell_yields.speaker: narrator
bindwell_yields.text: It was a long time before the needle answered. When he did, he only said: "Mind the stitches." But he got up.

bindwell_hub.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_hub.text: Don't look at me like that. I'm not here to be forgiven. I'm here because the binding's rotten and nobody else alive knows the stitch.

bindwell_hub.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_hub.text: Every page I open again, I'll have to look at what got left outside it. That's the price. I'll pay it.

bindwell_hub.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_hub.text: Don't. Go and do the thing you came up the mountain not saying.

bindwell_hub_repeat.speaker: bindwell
bindwell_hub_repeat.text: Kettle stitch. Over, under, back through the last. It holds because every stitch is tied to the one before it. Remember that, fox.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: narrator
peaks_lowpoint.text: Past the workshop the snow came sideways, and there was nothing to do but get behind a rock and light what they had and wait.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: corrugate
peaks_lowpoint.text: Say it, fox. You've been not saying it since the harbour. It's heavier than I am, and I'm wet.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: patch
peaks_lowpoint.text: The night of the flood I was on the Weather Page. With Drizzle. We were always together. She'd follow me anywhere. I liked that she would.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: patch
peaks_lowpoint.text: The water came over the edge of the page, and she was smaller than me, and slower, and she held onto my tail.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: patch
peaks_lowpoint.text: And I pulled. I didn't pull her up. I pulled away. The tail tore off in her hands and I ran, and I didn't look back, and I heard her calling all the way down.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: patch
peaks_lowpoint.text: Every story I've told since is about something that took my tail. Storms. Dragons. The moon. It was never anything. It was me getting away.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: patch
peaks_lowpoint.text: And she went down into the ink and came up as the Sogg. That's what's drowning the book. That's what I left behind. Bindwell sewed a door shut. I didn't even need a door.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: corrugate
peaks_lowpoint.text: I'm not going to tell you it's fine. It isn't.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: corrugate
peaks_lowpoint.text: But you came back. Nobody else from that page came back. You came all the way up here, to the worst of it, to the top, to her.

peaks_lowpoint.speaker: narrator
peaks_lowpoint.text: When the wind dropped they went on, up, to the top of the spine, where the Sogg was waiting. This time nobody told a story on the way.
